about: The tool’s own Engineering cards for 339 1st Ave E, Vancouver (the data centre alone, air-cooled, as the cards size it), read off the rendered cards by the interface on 21 Nov 2026 for the landing page. Each figure keeps its card and label; sources and confidence are on those cards. Nothing typed.

recovered.label: heat recovered from the air-cooled hall (option A)

offered.label: heat offered, after the heat pump

carbon.v: 45–119 t CO₂e/yr at 18.1 g/kWh (NIR, 2024, preliminary); 57–150 at the BC Government’s 22.8 g/kWh (imports included)
carbon.label: Carbon of the heat pump power

withinWorth.label: within the heat’s worth, or depend

lead6.v: Air cooling is picked: one heat pump lifts all the hall’s heat. A 2.5 MW hall could offer 11,300–19,700 MWh a year. At today’s prices that heat costs more to deliver than it is worth.
lead6.label: card lead

lead7.v: 1009 buildings lie within 3,000 m. None costs less to connect than its heat is worth at today’s prices. The full version also counts commercial and apartment buildings from a licensed assessment list.
lead7.label: card lead
